nodes.description: Bone is added from the endosteal surface inward: the cranial diploe is lost, long-bone diaphyses and the pelvis sclerose, and the mandible thickens and loses its antegonial notches. Because the deposition is endosteal, the marrow cavity narrows while the external contour is largely preserved.

evidence.reference_title: Six novel missense mutations in the LDL receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5) gene in different conditions with an increased bone density.
evidence.snippet: Thirteen of these were confirmed as polymorphisms, but six novel missense mutations (D111Y, G171R, A214T, A214V, A242T, and T253I) are most likely disease causing.

evidence.reference_title: High bone density due to a mutation in LDL-receptor-related protein 5.
evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function mutations in the gene for low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5), which acts in the Wnt signaling pathway, have been shown to cause osteoporosis-pseudoglioma.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants clustered in the amino-terminal first beta-propeller of LRP5, before the first EGF-like domain. The same small region accounts for high bone density across several diagnoses that were historically kept apart.

evidence.reference_title: Six novel missense mutations in the LDL receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5) gene in different conditions with an increased bone density.
evidence.snippet: Like the previously reported mutation (G171V) that causes the high-bone-mass phenotype, all mutations are located in the aminoterminal part of the gene, before the first epidermal growth factor-like domain.

evidence.reference_title: High bone density due to a mutation in LDL-receptor-related protein 5.
evidence.snippet: Affected members of the kindred had a mutation in this gene, with valine substituted for glycine at codon 171 (LRP5V171).

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous first-propeller missense alleles that block sclerostin and DKK1 inhibition of the receptor. The gain of function is in the receptor's escape from regulation, not in raised ligand or raised receptor abundance.

nodes.description: The mutant receptor no longer responds to the two secreted Wnt inhibitors that normally restrain bone formation. Knock-in mice carrying the human p.G171V and p.A214V alleles are protected from osteopenia induced by overexpressing either inhibitor, which is the in vivo demonstration of the same mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: High Bone Mass-Causing Mutant LRP5 Receptors Are Resistant to Endogenous Inhibitors In Vivo.
evidence.snippet: We observed that the (8kb) Dmp1-SOST transgene significantly lowered whole-body bone mineral density (BMD), bone mineral content (BMC), femoral and vertebral trabecular bone volume fraction (BV/TV), and periosteal bone-formation rate (BFR) in wild-type mice but not in mice with Lrp5 p.G171V and p.A214V alleles.

evidence.snippet: The (2.3kb) Col1a1-Dkk1 transgene significantly lowered whole-body BMD, BMC, and vertebral BV/TV in wild-type mice and affected p.A214V mice more than p.G171V mice.

nodes.description: Knock-in mice carrying the human HBM alleles, crossed with transgenics overexpressing SOST in osteocytes or DKK1 in osteoblasts and osteocytes. The design tests inhibitor resistance in a living skeleton rather than in a reporter assay.

nodes.description: Canonical Wnt/beta-catenin output in the osteoblast lineage is raised because the receptor is deaf to its inhibitors, not because ligand is more abundant. The modifier here is GAIN_OF_FUNCTION rather than INCREASED for that reason: the pathway is running outside its normal regulatory constraints, which is a qualitative change, not a quantitative one.
